decisions.reason: Approving Inter and the thicker body-text treatment does not change the policy against empty article endings or the accepted methods for filling those areas.
The body-font approval does not change the required upload format, even page-count rule, or two-page spread behavior.
The source decision concerns article body typography and does not alter category content, placement, or label styling.
The approved body-font treatment does not affect the required shape or size of author photographs.
Changing article body typography does not modify the requirement for accurate final article page references on the cover.
The typography approval does not change the requirement to complete the table of contents from finalized pagination.
The source decision does not alter author-name, author-photo, identity-matching, source, or placement requirements.
Approval of Inter and its body-text treatment does not change the prohibition on using red for the Dorian Vale article.
The source decision concerns article body text and does not change advertisement clarity or rendering requirements.
The body-font choice does not alter which cover-mentioned articles must be included or how their placement is determined.
The typography decision does not change the Civic Lantern website as the source of article content.
The client approves a specific article body-font treatment but does not modify the broader polished, modern, brand-aligned visual-style requirement.
